title: Unified Configuration for E-commerce Micro-frontends
business: A retail platform managing dozens of independent micro-frontends built on Vite.
problem: Development teams face configuration drift where production build pipelines and test environments diverge, leading to 'works in dev but fails in test' scenarios that delay deployment cycles.
solution: By utilizing Vitest, the organization leverages the existing Vite configuration files directly within the test runner. This ensures that resolve aliases, environment variables, and plugin transformations are identical during both the build process and the execution of unit tests, eliminating environment-specific discrepancies.
steps: Install Vitest as a dev dependency in the root of the micro-frontend project.
Configure the vitest.config.ts file to extend or import the existing vite.config.ts settings.
Define test suites using the standard Vitest API, ensuring compatibility with existing Jest-like syntax.
Integrate the vitest command into the package.json scripts to trigger watch mode during development.
Execute tests using the shared resolution pipeline to validate component behavior against production-like settings.
outcome: Teams achieve higher confidence in test results, as the testing environment perfectly mirrors the production build pipeline, reducing the frequency of integration bugs.
limitation: Because Vitest relies on the Vite pipeline, complex custom plugins that are strictly tied to build-time assets may require conditional logic to avoid execution errors during testing. Developers can check for this by inspecting the vitest.config.ts file to ensure that plugins are correctly guarded or mocked when the environment is set to 'test'.
